claim: Harry sold B.Fernandes and bought Palmer, preferring Chelsea's most explosive short-term pick over building longer-term squad structure ahead of Hull (h) and Brentford (a).
quote: I sold Bruno Fernandez and I bought Cole Palmer.

claim: Harry says Morgan Rogers might suit long-term squad structure better alongside Saka or B.Fernandes, but for just a couple of good fixtures (Hull home, Brentford away) he wanted the most explosive Chelsea player, Palmer.
quote: I do want the most explosive Chelsea player who I believe is Cole Palmer.

claim: Harry sold Rodon and bought Muharemović, made on Friday evening ahead of a forecast price drop for Rodon and before Arsenal's team news was known.
quote: I bought Rodon out and I bought Mhmic in.

claim: Harry picked Muharemović over Konsa or White because he rates him much better for defensive contribution points and slightly more attacking threat, with home fixtures against Newcastle and Crystal Palace before a gameweek six wildcard.
quote: He's much better for Defcon than both Ezri Konza and Ben White and maybe has slightly more attacking threat.

claim: Harry made the Rodon-to-Muharemović swap without yet knowing whether Timber or Mosquera would be in Arsenal's squad that weekend, saying he might have picked an Arsenal defender instead had he known both would be out.
quote: I didn't know whether Timber was going to be in the Arsenal squad and whether Moscara was going to be as well at the weekend

claim: Harry sold Tzolis and bought Gibbs-White rather than tripling up on Chelsea attack, since he already owns João Pedro and had just bought Palmer.
quote: I sold Solace and I bought Morgan Gibbs White.

claim: Harry chose Gibbs-White over Morgan Rogers, liking Forest's next fixtures (Villa away, Coventry home) with Villa carrying Champions League fatigue, and rating Gibbs-White as the clear penalty taker and main open-play goal threat for Forest.
quote: I like Gibbs White for the next two set pieces penalties and their main open play goal threat

claim: Harry expects Gibbs-White to be on penalties for Nottingham Forest.
quote: Gibbs White definitely is.

claim: Harry confirms Palmer took and scored a penalty for Chelsea in the Wednesday Carabao Cup win over Leeds, and expects him to be on penalties for Chelsea with João Pedro not having been on the pitch.
quote: He also took a penalty. Jedro wasn't on the pitch, but I expect Palmer to be on pens.

claim: Harry's gameweek four captain is Palmer with João Pedro as vice, choosing Chelsea's home fixture against Hull over Haaland away at Man Utd.
quote: Palmer is my captain at the moment for gameweek four with J Pedro getting the vice captaincy.

claim: Harry still rates Haaland as a good captain option but leans Chelsea because Hull have not conceded a Premier League goal yet are third for big chances conceded and 14th for xGC, plus Palmer's likely penalty duty.
quote: Chelsea's attack does tend to perform pretty well this season at home especially... the fact that he's likely on penalties

claim: After watching Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup with Palmer coming off the bench to score twice including a penalty, Harry says Palmer will almost certainly be his captain, with João Pedro (who had a full rest Wednesday) as vice.
quote: Palmer is in. I'm almost certain he will have the captain armband. I think Jal Pedro will be my vice.

claim: Harry notes João Pedro had a full rest in the Wednesday Carabao Cup match against Leeds.
quote: I know Japro had a full rest on Wednesday evening

claim: Harry says Chelsea rotated heavily in the first half of the Wednesday Carabao Cup match, which makes him confident Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are all set to start at home to Hull in gameweek four.
quote: which makes me think absolutely Palmer Rogers Ja Pedro are all absolutely set to start in gameweek four at home to Hull

claim: Harry says Fofana and Hato, cheap Chelsea defenders, are also probably going to start at home to Hull in gameweek four, but he's still not sure he'd invest in Chelsea defensively.
quote: cheap defenders if you wanted a Chelsea defender are also probably going to start at home to Hull in gameweek four

claim: Harry notes Morgan Rogers picked up four assists in the second half of the Wednesday Carabao Cup win over Leeds after being subbed on alongside Palmer, which makes him wonder if Rogers over Gibbs-White would have been the better transfer.
quote: Morgan Rogers picked up four assists in that game in the second half once he was subbed on alongside Cole Palmer

claim: Despite second-guessing Gibbs-White vs Rogers after the cup match, Harry says he will not activate his wildcard to fix it; Palmer stays in his team regardless.
quote: I'm not going to activate my wild card to rectify it, but maybe I should have gone for Morgan Rogers over Morgan Gibbs White.

claim: Harry starts Mbeumo at home to Manchester City ahead of Gomez away to Coventry, rating Mbeumo's form and price above Gomez despite Man Utd's Thursday Champions League fixture giving City extra rest before the game.
quote: I've been so impressed by Bronnen Burmo out on that right wing... I do plan on starting Brian and Burmo even though he's playing against Manchester City.

claim: Harry cites Mbeumo as second for expected goals among all midfielders in the game.
quote: He's second for expected goals amongst all midfielders in the entire game.

claim: Harry's gameweek three standout was Mbeumo, whom he decided not to sell for Cherki, meaning he avoided buying a Man City midfielder and rolled a transfer into gameweek four.
quote: My star of the game week was Brian and Burma, who I decided not to sell and buy Churkey.

claim: Harry starts Verbruggen over Kinsky, judging Coventry weaker going forward than an impressive Everton attack, despite Coventry being at home and Everton away.
quote: I'm just about favoring going for Vugan despite the fact I did it this way around last week and got the decision wrong.

claim: Harry starts Calafiori despite a slight risk from Arsenal's away trip to Sunderland, saying you always play your Arsenal defenders.
quote: There is of course a slight risk with Sunland away at the weekend, but I'm going to start with him. You always play your ass defenders.

claim: Harry calls Ajer his weakest defender going into gameweek four, away at Bournemouth, expecting little beyond maybe a defensive contribution point.
quote: He was almost certainly my weakest defender going into gameweek four.

claim: Harry's new defender Muharemović plays at home to Newcastle in the Monday night gameweek four fixture, which he likes for having an extra player in the last game of the round.
quote: my new transfer in was Mhmic at home to Newcastle. He is of course the Monday night fixture which is always nice

claim: Harry says Solanke (referred to as Dominic) isn't currently his favoured pick, though he could have had a penalty in gameweek three that was ruled out for a marginal offside, which would have made him feel more positive about him.
quote: he could have had a penalty in gameweek three, which was ruled out for a very marginal offside

claim: Harry reports Solanke and Calvert-Lewin both scored in Wednesday's midweek cup matches, calling it a great night for his FPL team.
quote: Dominic Sabos live scoring Calbert Lewen scoring. It's been a great midweek for my FPL team.

claim: Harry's starting front three for gameweek four are Haaland away at Man Utd, Calvert-Lewin at home to Newcastle, and João Pedro at home to Hull.
quote: Erling Harland away at Man United... Caluan leads at home to Newcastle and then Jao Pedra home to Hull.

claim: Harry is not playing his wildcard in gameweek four; he plans to save it for gameweek six, right before a three-week international break, arguing his team doesn't need drastic changes yet and a month of team news could still change his plans.
quote: I can save in gameweek five, roll the transfer next week, and wild card over a three-week international break, which still just feels such a nice opportunity to do it.

claim: Harry has already used his Bench Boost and Triple Captain chips this season (Triple Captain on Haaland in gameweek three for 9 points), leaving Wildcard and Free Hit still available.
quote: I have already used my wild card, sorry, my bench boost and my triple captain in the wild card potentially to be played in the next few weeks.

claim: Harry says the wildcard change he'd most want is another Arsenal defender in place of Verbruggen or Ajer, doubling up his Arsenal defense, though he doesn't view it as a drastic enough need to wildcard now.
quote: I would have another Arsenal defender over either Vugan or Ayair. And absolutely. Would I rather double ass defense over both of those this week? Probably.

claim: Harry says his defensive gamble depends on Arsenal not keeping back-to-back clean sheets away at Sunderland and away at Brighton before he wildcards in gameweek six.
quote: as long as they don't keep back-to-back clean sheets against Sunland and Brighton

claim: Harry tells viewers there's a world where triple-captaining Palmer against Hull in gameweek four could be considered, even though Hull have been strong defensively.
quote: if you've got your triple captain, I know Hull have been great, but I do think there is a world where you will consider it.

claim: Harry says if Chelsea attack in gameweek four against Hull the way they did in the second half of Wednesday's Carabao Cup win, they should have no problem breaking down Hull's previously miserly Premier League defense.
quote: if we attack like we did in the second half in that game against Hull at the weekend, I don't expect us to have any sorts of problems
